title: Best Sci-Fi Series Streaming in India
intro: Science fiction on streaming has stopped being a prestige novelty and started being the genre where the best writers are working. These are the series available in India that actually earn the genre tag - where the speculative premise is load-bearing, not decorative, and the ideas go somewhere the plot alone cannot.

picks.title: Dark
picks.one_line: German time-loop horror set across four generations of a small town - the most rigorously constructed time-travel narrative on television, and strangely beautiful.

picks.title: Stranger Things
picks.one_line: A Spielbergian monster-of-the-week homage that accumulated genuine stakes across its run - Season 4 is its highest-budget and most ambitious.

picks.title: Severance
picks.one_line: Office workers whose work and personal selves are surgically separated - a metaphor so precise it generates entire plot mechanics and a look unlike anything else on television.

picks.title: Fallout
picks.one_line: The video-game adaptation that solved the adaptation problem by treating lore as atmosphere and character as content - three leads, three tones, one thrillingly chaotic story.

picks.title: The Last of Us
picks.one_line: Post-pandemic father-daughter road trip with a grief study underneath the fungal-apocalypse surface - Episode 3 ('Long Long Time') may be the best hour of TV in this decade.

picks.title: Andor
picks.one_line: Star Wars stripped of myth and spectacle until only the politics of resistance remain - Tony Gilroy writes imperial bureaucracy like he invented the genre.

picks.title: Black Mirror
picks.one_line: Charlie Brooker's technology-horror anthology has uneven seasons but the peak episodes - 'San Junipero', 'USS Callister', 'White Bear' - are permanently lodged in cultural memory.

faq.q: Is Dark too complicated to follow without taking notes?
faq.a: Season 1 is followable without notes - the show earns its complexity gradually. By Season 2 a family tree chart becomes genuinely helpful; Netflix's companion site has one. The investment pays: Dark's plotting is tighter than nearly any sci-fi series that has attempted time travel, and the emotional core is straightforward even when the timeline is not.

faq.q: What's the best sci-fi for someone who doesn't usually watch the genre?
faq.a: Severance, because it's functionally an office comedy-thriller in its first two episodes before the premise locks in. Black Mirror works episode-by-episode without commitment - start with 'San Junipero' or 'USS Callister'. The Last of Us is the strongest case for genre crossover: it's primarily a character study about parenthood, grief, and love.
